text:
Erik Karlsson is 36, leads the Penguins in scoring by Hockey Hot Stove's Ryan Wilson's count, and just moved into the top ten all time in points by a defenseman. Three Norris Trophies in, he's still the engine of Pittsburgh's offense: 16 points in 16 games, half of them on the power play, 23:17 a night.

The trouble is everything around those points. Pittsburgh has won two of his last ten games, and at 5v5 the Penguins get just 45% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 12 points worse than when he sits. That's a long way from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him 23rd among 215 defensemen at 2.3 wins above replacement against top-3% competition.

His shooting is running hot (11.1% against our expected range of about 6 to 9.5%), so expect fewer goals. The playmaking is real: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile among defensemen in primary shot assists. And the rental talk has started, with NHLTradeRumor.com already sketching what he'd cost Toronto. A point producer on a team losing this much will keep hearing his name.
headline: Karlsson keeps producing as Pittsburgh keeps losing
